regulatory_note: US Coast Guard Subchapter T inspection; Florida clean-marina and manatee/no-wake zones favor zero-emission, low-wake operation; shallow-draft barrier-island navigation requires route discipline.
seasonality: Strongly seasonal (Nov–Apr snowbird peak); the Gulf coast is calmer than the Atlantic side, favoring all-electric operation most of the year. Hurricane season (Jun–Nov) is the main disruption.
signature_routes: Fort Myers ↔ Boca Grande (Useppa / Cabbage Key)
summary: The southwest Florida Gulf coast is one of the densest affluent boating markets in the US, with calmer water than the Atlantic side and a string of barrier islands reachable today only by causeway or boat. Naples — the wealthiest metro per capita in Florida — Marco Island, Bonita and Estero anchor the south; Fort Myers, Sanibel, Captiva and Boca Grande / Gasparilla anchor the north. Causeway congestion to Sanibel (and its post-Ian rebuild) plus the no-bridge access to Useppa and Cabbage Key make a fast, sheltered water layer attractive for both resort transfer and affluent residential commuting.
tagline: Southwest Florida's calm Gulf-coast boating belt — Naples, Marco and the barrier islands — affluent, year-round and sheltered.
